basis: Perivascular glomus-cell proliferation associated with dilated vascular spaces; a consistent skin or subcutaneous origin is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: none: glomangiomatosis can involve deep soft tissues; the supplied definition does not establish a predominantly cutaneous origin.

basis: Congenital contractures and characteristic ptosis define the syndrome; ptosis occurs in 7/10. Tongue atrophy directly affects oral tissue in 7/7.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic asymmetric ptosis is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 7/10 patients.

basis: Heterogeneous umbrella of lysosomal metabolic disorders; neurologic damage varies by subtype, without an established patient-level frequency across the group.

decisions.neurologic: none: estimates that many lysosomal disease types are neurologic do not establish involvement in most patients across this heterogeneous umbrella.

basis: Gonadotropin deficiency defines the endocrine disorder; anosmia is a defining Kallmann feature and occurs in 4/4 annotated patients.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the Kallmann syndrome parent establishes defining olfactory dysfunction, supported by anosmia in 4/4 patients.

basis: Vertebral segmentation and rib defects define the skeletal disease; explicit fucoglycosan-synthesis ancestry identifies an inherited glycosylation disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the supplied fucoglycosan-synthesis-disorder ancestry establishes a metabolic mechanism, beyond the LFNG gene name alone.

basis: Sphingolipid-biosynthesis disorder causing neuropathy; ulcers (4/7) follow insensate injury rather than direct skin disease; osteomyelitis (3/5) is a separate infection.

decisions.dermatologic: none: ulcers affect 4/7 but arise through trauma to insensate tissue, rather than direct cutaneous damage by the disease process.

basis: HPO: intellectual disability, hearing loss and cytopenias/coagulopathy each 30-79%; hepatic dysfunction and chorioretinitis also frequent but omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia, thrombocytopenia and coagulation dysfunction each occur in 30-79% per HPO; retained for direct blood dysfunction.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic dysfunction is annotated at 30-79%, but omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of neurologic, hearing and blood involvement.

basis: Developmental impairment, epilepsy and brain atrophy define disease; strabismus (4/6) and nystagmus (3/6) do not establish direct damage to ocular structures.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus (4/6) and nystagmus (3/6) establish ocular motor abnormalities, but not direct eye damage distinct from the neurologic disorder.

basis: Hearing loss, heart defects and cleft palate define structural disease; developmental delay is also explicit in the definition and retained within the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is an explicit defining oral malformation, prioritized with the named hearing and heart defects within the three-primary cap.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay is explicit in the definition, meeting the major-feature exception; retained after the three primary slots are filled.

basis: Extreme insulin resistance with characteristic skin/nail disease; developmental disability and dental abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Recurrent infections do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic persistent skin, hair and nail abnormalities help define the syndrome, supported by hypertrichosis ancestry and HPO frequencies of 30-79%.
